Title: HU-M3 — Question-closed participant state
Description:
## Parent

Local plan: `mobile/plans/post-hu-34a-mobile-trivia-breakdown.md` (section `HU-M3`).
Upstream slice: `DES-82` (HU-M1 — active question display). Backend close facts from `DES-45` (HU-33B).

## What to build

Keep the participant experience coherent after a trivia question window closes. This slice owns the surface that `HU-M1` deliberately left to a later slice: reacting to the `QuestionClosed` broadcast (`QuestionClosedNotificationDto` via the `QuestionClosed` SignalR method).

This is **close-state UI only** — submit and post-submit waiting state live in `HU-M2` (blocked by `HU-34A` / `DES-46`). Until `HU-M2` lands, "question closed" simply means: no more interaction with the just-closed question, and the app should look for the next snapshot.

Backend surfaces consumed:

* `QuestionClosed` broadcast → `QuestionClosedNotificationDto` (`LiveSessionId`, `QuestionIndex`, `ClosedAt`, `WasExpiredByTimer`).
* REST `GET /sessions/{liveSessionId}/participants/timer` → re-fetch to discover the next `ActiveQuestionSnapshotDto` (or null = waiting/advancing).
* `SessionStateChanged` for terminal transitions (`Finished`/`Cancelled`) that end participation.

## Mobile scope

* "Question closed" state with the answer controls immediately non-interactive (no longer accepts selection, even when `HU-M2` lands).
* After a `QuestionClosed` broadcast, re-fetch the participant-timer snapshot to discover the next question or the waiting state. The data path must already exist from `HU-M1`; this slice wires the trigger.
* Clear visual distinction between:
  * this team already answered (only knowable once `HU-M2` ships; until then, this branch is unreachable and the state is simply "closed")
  * question closed before this team answered (the only observable close variant until `HU-M2`)
  * waiting for the next question or substage advancement
* Reconnect into a session whose active question is already closed restores the correct closed/waiting state from the snapshot rather than rendering a stale active-question view.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On `QuestionClosed` broadcast, the screen transitions out of the active-question view and locks any answer controls.
- [ ] After close, the participant-timer snapshot is re-fetched and the next active question (or a waiting state) is rendered accordingly.
- [ ] Reconnect into a closed question restores the closed/waiting state from the snapshot without manual refresh.
- [ ] Terminal session states (`Finished`, `Cancelled`) end participation cleanly and surface the "session no longer accepting participation" empty state from `HU-M1`.

## Blocked by

* `DES-82` (HU-M1 — active question display + countdown)

Title: HU-M2 — Submit first answer from mobile
Description:
## Parent

Local plan: `mobile/plans/post-hu-34a-mobile-trivia-breakdown.md` (section `HU-M2`). *(Filename predates the 2026-07-09 merge; the HU it describes is now* `HU-34`*.)*

Backend dependency: `DES-46` (HU-34 — first-valid-answer registration) shipped in PR #133 (2026-07-10). **Its answer contract is frozen by the** `EN-M1` **spike (**`DES-81`**)** — this slice consumes that spike's contract note; it does not verify backend shapes itself.

## What to build

Allow a participant team to submit one trivia answer from the mobile client during an active question, wired to the real HU-34 first-valid-answer contract as frozen in `DES-81`'s note under `mobile/docs/`. This is the participant side of HU-34's "any authenticated team member can submit the answer for the active question".

Picks up where `HU-M1` (`DES-82`) left the options visibly non-interactive and where `HU-M3` (`DES-83`) locks them on close.

## Contract (already frozen — see `DES-81`)

Consume the shapes `DES-81` typed and recorded; do **not** re-derive them from the backend. For reference:

* Submit — `POST /sessions/{liveSessionId}/participants/answers` (`Participant` policy). Request: `TeamId`, `TriviaSubstageSnapshotId`, `QuestionSequenceOrder`, `SelectedOptionSequenceOrder`, `Token?`. Accepted (200): acceptance metadata only — no correctness/points.
* Rejection `reasonCode` slugs: `late-trivia-answer`, `duplicate-trivia-answer`, `trivia-answer-requires-active-question`, `trivia-answer-requires-active-session`, `trivia-answer-requires-trivia-substage`, `invalid-trivia-answer-option`, `answer-submitter-is-not-session-participant`.
* ⚠️ `TriviaSubstageSnapshotId` is required by submit but is **not** on the active-question broadcast/snapshot. `DES-81` picks where the client sources it — follow that decision here; do not invent a second one.
* `TeamAnswered` is operator-only. This client does not consume it.

If any shape is missing from `DES-81`'s note, that is a gap in the spike — raise it there, do not re-verify against the backend in this slice.

## Test identity — drive against the seeded participant

Drive and verify this slice against the `participant` account already seeded in `backend/deploy/keycloak/import/umbral-realm.json` (`emailVerified: true`, realm role `Participant`). That account is a real, sign-in-capable participant — enough to build and verify submit end to end.

`GH #143` **(participant self-registration) is NOT a blocker for this slice.** It only governs whether a *real end user* can create their own account from the app; the submit contract is identical whether the identity came from the seed or from hosted registration. Do not wait on it, and do not wire this slice to it. (`#143` is itself blocked by `#141`/SMTP and lives dead-last in the identity track.)

## Mobile scope

* Option selection UI (single-select on the active question's options).
* Submit action wired to the frozen contract.
* Local pending state while the submission is in flight.
* Interaction lock immediately after a successful submission so the team cannot accidentally double-submit while awaiting the backend result.
* Rejection handling mapped to participant-facing UI for each `reasonCode` above (late, duplicate, invalid session/question state, wrong substage, invalid option, forbidden/wrong-team) plus network failure.
* Hand-off into the `HU-M3` waiting / closed states on success and on close.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A team can submit exactly one answer from the app during an active question, using the `DES-81`-frozen contract.
- [ ] The screen prevents accidental double-submit while awaiting the backend result (pending state + interaction lock).
- [ ] Each backend rejection `reasonCode` maps to a clear participant-facing message; no invented domain rules.
- [ ] A successful submission transitions cleanly into the `HU-M3` "answer submitted" waiting state.
- [ ] Submit is disabled while the question is closed (integration with `DES-83`).

## Blocked by

* `DES-82` (HU-M1 — active question display) — option UI lives on top of HU-M1.
* `DES-81` (EN-M1 — contract spike) — freezes the submit contract this slice consumes. *(The* `DES-46` *dependency is discharged transitively:* [DES-46](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-46/hu-34-registro-y-rechazo-de-respuestas-de-equipo-en-trivia) *shipped,* [DES-81](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-81/en-m1-mobile-trivia-contract-spike-display-submit) *froze its contract.* `GH #143` *is not a blocker — see §Test identity.)*

## Notas

Updated 2026-07-10: the "backend surface assumed by this slice, to be verified against HU-34 output before implementation" clause was removed. That verification is now `DES-81`'s job — the spike widened to freeze the submit contract alongside the display contract once `DES-46` shipped. This slice consumes a frozen note instead of re-deriving a contract mid-implementation.

Title: HU-34 - Registro y rechazo de respuestas de equipo en trivia
Description:
'> **Forma de evidencia de trivia.** La respuesta del equipo a la pregunta activa es la *evidencia* de las subetapas de trivia (`TriviaAnswerSubmission`), una de las formas concretas del umbral `EvidenceSubmission` (la otra es el QR de búsqueda del tesoro, HU-31). El intake y la validación de contexto comunes viven en HU-29/HU-30A; esta HU especializa el registro de la primera respuesta válida y su rechazo (tardías o repetidas), y conserva su tipo y evento propios. Ver ADR-0010 (en revisión).

> **Fusión 2026-07-09.** Absorbe HU-34B ([DES-47](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-47/hu-34b-rechazo-de-respuestas-tardias-o-repetidas-en-trivia)). Aceptación y rechazo son las dos ramas de una misma escritura — un guard first-write-wins, no dos entregables. El rechazo es una preocupación de validador, no un segundo handler. Ver `backend/docs/ab-ticket-merge-validation-handoff-2026-07-09.md`.

## What to build

Aceptar la primera respuesta válida enviada por cualquier integrante autenticado del equipo para la pregunta activa, como la forma de evidencia de trivia (`TriviaAnswerSubmission`), y rechazar de forma explicada las respuestas tardías o los intentos repetidos.

## Acceptance criteria

Title: HU-15 follow-up — Archive-time enforcement for quizzes referenced by active missions
Description:
## What to build

Proactive **archive-time enforcement** in mission-design so a trivia quiz that is referenced by an **active** mission cannot silently become a dead reference. Today archival is allowed unconditionally, leaving the mission pointing at a non-published quiz.

This is **Phase 3** of the "published-quiz readiness gap" remediation, explicitly deferred out of the fix plan because it needs a new capability and a product decision (see Context below). Phases 1 & 2 (reactive readiness + fail-fast at session creation) close the create path; Phase 3 closes the gap at its source.

## Background — the readiness gap

Repro: an operator selects a **published** quiz into a trivia substage (allowed), activates the mission (allowed), then **archives** the quiz. The mission stays `Ready`; a session can be created whose trivia substage resolves to **zero questions**, surfacing only at play time as `TriviaSubstageSnapshotMustContainQuestionsException`.

Phases 1 & 2 make the system *react* to this downstream (readiness re-evaluates publication; snapshot build rejects an empty trivia substage). Phase 3 *prevents* it at the moment of archival.

## Product decision required (resolve before building)

Pick the archival semantics — this is a quiz-lifecycle UX call, not an implementation detail:

* **(A) Block archival** of a quiz while it is referenced by any active mission (operator must first swap the selection / deactivate the mission), **or**
* **(B) Cascade**: allow archival but automatically move affected missions out of `Ready`/`Active` (deactivate) and notify.

Record the decision in an ADR or the canon ledger addendum before writing the final AC.

## Missing capability

This needs a **quiz → mission inverse query** ("which active missions reference this quiz?") that does not exist today — `IMissionRepository` is CRUD-only. New infrastructure, not a small add.

## Acceptance criteria (pending the decision above)

- [ ] Archivar un quiz referenciado por una misión activa aplica la semántica elegida (bloqueo **o** cascada de desactivación), de forma consistente.
- [ ] Existe una consulta inversa quiz→misiones que identifica las misiones activas que referencian un quiz dado.
- [ ] El handler de archivado (`ArchiveTriviaQuizCommandHandler` / `TriviaQuizArchivedEvent`) consume esa consulta y reacciona según la decisión de producto.
- [ ] Cobertura: unit del nuevo guard/handler + integración del flujo seleccionar→activar→archivar.

## Context (cited)

* `MissionActivationPolicy.EvaluateTrivia()` is structural-only and cannot see `TriviaQuiz.Status`.
* Publication is checked only at selection time (`TriviaQuizSelectionGuard.EnsurePublishedSelectionAsync`); nothing re-validates on archival.
* `ArchiveTriviaQuizCommandHandler` raises `TriviaQuizArchivedEvent`, which has **no** handler that touches missions.

## Blocked by

[DES-22](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-22/hu-15-creacion-de-sesion-de-mision-desde-mision-activa) (HU-15) — Phases 1 & 2 of the fix must land first. See plan `plans/fix-published-quiz-readiness-gap.md` (Phase 3 section).

Title: HU-10A - Estructura jerárquica de misiones
Description:
## What to build

Permitir modelar la estructura de una misión como un árbol acotado de nodos (`MissionNode`) con la jerarquía `Stage → Substage → Clue`. El dominio (no los handlers) hace cumplir qué hijos admite cada nodo (patrón Composite).

Cada `Substage` declara su `SubstagePlayMode` (`TreasureHunt` o `Trivia`), que determina su contenido jugable:

* **TreasureHunt**: la subetapa posee `Target`s ordenados. El `Target` es el objetivo QR-validado (progresión basada en targets); **no es un nodo de la jerarquía**, es contenido propiedad de la subetapa.
* **Trivia**: la subetapa referencia un único quiz publicado por identidad (el quiz completo).

Una `Clue` es guía **opcional** del jugador y puede asociarse a lo sumo a un `Target` de su **misma** subetapa; la asociación es solo guía y nunca resuelve ni avanza el `Target` ni la subetapa.

> Nota de modelo: el `nodeType` implementado es `{Stage, Substage, Clue}`. El `Target` se modela como entidad propiedad de la `Substage` en modo `TreasureHunt`, **no** como un tipo de nodo. (Corrige el texto previo, que omitía `SubstagePlayMode` y `Target`.)

## Acceptance criteria

### Jerarquía y contención (estructura)

- [ ] La misión permite registrar nodos `Stage`, `Substage` y `Clue` dentro de la jerarquía `Stage → Substage → Clue`.
- [ ] Una `Stage` solo admite hijos `Substage`; el sistema rechaza una `Clue` directa bajo una `Stage`.
- [ ] Una `Substage` solo admite hijos `Clue`; el sistema rechaza una `Substage` anidada dentro de otra `Substage`.
- [ ] Una `Clue` es nodo hoja: el sistema rechaza cualquier intento de asignarle nodos hijos.
- [ ] Cada `Stage` debe contener al menos una `Substage` para considerarse lista para runtime.
- [ ] Todo rechazo informa explícitamente que la estructura es inválida, indicando el tipo de nodo padre y el tipo de hijo no permitido.

### Modo de juego y contenido de la subetapa (canon)

- [ ] Cada `Substage` tiene exactamente un `SubstagePlayMode` (`TreasureHunt` o `Trivia`) fijado al crearse.
- [ ] En `TreasureHunt`, la subetapa posee `Target`s ordenados (objetivo QR-validado) y un puntaje de ganador; las operaciones de `Target` se rechazan si la subetapa no está en `TreasureHunt`.
- [ ] En `Trivia`, la subetapa referencia un único quiz publicado por identidad; las operaciones de `Target` no aplican.
- [ ] Una `Clue` puede asociarse a lo sumo a un `Target` de su misma subetapa; la asociación es opcional, es solo guía, y nunca resuelve ni avanza el `Target` ni la subetapa.

Title: HARDENING - TargetSnapshot.Score es int? vestigial: DES-86 expandió la nulabilidad y nunca la contrajo
Description:
## What to build

Contraer la nulabilidad de `Score` en `session-operations-service`, de punta a punta. El `int?` es un residuo del paso *expand* de [DES-86](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-86/refactor-puntaje-por-objetivo-per-target-scorevalue-en-lugar-de-winner): nunca hubo un paso *contract* que lo cerrara.

> **Reescrito 2026-07-10.** La versión original de este ticket afirmaba tres defectos. Solo uno existe. Ver §"Lo que este ticket NO hace" — el recorte no es cosmético, dos de los tres ACs originales violaban ADR-0015 o describían un bug inexistente.

## Estado actual (verificado en código, 2026-07-10, post-[DES-86](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-86/refactor-puntaje-por-objetivo-per-target-scorevalue-en-lugar-de-winner))

**El productor emite** `int` **no-nulable.** `backend/services/mission-design-service/src/Application/Dtos/Missions/MissionRuntimePlanDto.cs:25` expone `int Score`. El valor nace de un `ScoreValue`, cuyo `Create` (`.../Domain/ValueObjects/ScoreValue.cs:20-33`) rechaza `<= 0` y `> 100`.

**El relay lo recibe como** `int?`**.** La nulabilidad se propaga por toda la cadena:

| Sitio | Hoy |
| -- | -- |
| `session-operations-service/src/Infrastructure/Integrations/MissionDesign/MissionRuntimeSource.cs:112` | `int? Score` |
| `session-operations-service/src/Application/Dtos/Sessions/MissionRuntimeDto.cs:25` | `int? Score` |
| `session-operations-service/src/Domain/ValueObjects/TargetSnapshot.cs:59` | `public int? Score { get; }` |
| `session-operations-service/src/Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/LiveSessionConfiguration.cs:244` | `.HasColumnName("score")`, sin `.IsRequired()` |
| Migración `20260710043112_AddPerTargetScoreDropSubstageWinnerScore` | `nullable: true` |

**El** `null` **no puede llegar por el cable.** No hay productor que lo emita. La rama que lo compensa existe solo por eso:

```csharp
// Domain/Entities/MissionRuntimeSnapshot.cs:139
if (substageTargets.Any(target => target.Score is null || target.Score.Value <= 0))
{
    throw new TreasureHuntTargetSnapshotScoreRequiredException();
}
```

**La asimetría vive dentro del mismo archivo.** En `MissionRuntimeDto.cs`, el lado de trivia ya lo hizo bien: `int? Score` (línea 25, target) contra `int ScoreValue` (línea 35, trivia). Mismo contraste en `MissionRuntimeSource.cs` (líneas 112 y 140).

## Why now

[DES-86](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-86/refactor-puntaje-por-objetivo-per-target-scorevalue-en-lugar-de-winner) hizo expand/contract sobre el modelo per-target. F1 ensanchó `session-operations` a `int?` para que conviviesen el escritor viejo y el nuevo; F3 contrajo `WinnerScore` pero nunca volvió por la nulabilidad. El tipo hoy admite un estado que ningún camino produce, y `MissionRuntimeSnapshot.cs:139` paga el costo de defenderse de él.

[DES-42](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-42/hu-31-escaneo-validacion-y-registro-server-side-de-objetivo-qr) (HU-31) va a leer este `Score` para poblar el payload de `TargetResolved`, y [DES-51](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-51/hu-37-ledger-de-puntaje-por-validaciones-respuestas-y-penalizaciones) (HU-37) lo va a acumular en `ScoreEntry`. Cuanto más abajo llegue el `int?`, más sitios tendrán que decidir qué hacer con un `null` que nunca ocurre.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TargetSnapshot.Score` pasa de `int?` a `int` no-nulable. **No** se introduce un `ScoreValue` propio de `SessionOperations` — ver §"Lo que este ticket NO hace".
- [ ] El constructor de `TargetSnapshot` (`TargetSnapshot.cs:15-45`, que hoy valida `TargetSnapshotId` y `SubstageSnapshotId` y **no toca** `score`) gana un guard estructural `score > 0`. Un `TargetSnapshot` con puntaje no-positivo debe ser inconstruible. Sin cota superior.
- [ ] `MissionRuntimeDto.cs:25` y `MissionRuntimeSource.cs:112` pasan a `int`, alineándose con el `int ScoreValue` que el lado de trivia ya usa en ambos archivos.
- [ ] `LiveSessionConfiguration.cs:244` declara `.IsRequired()`.
- [ ] Una migración vuelve `score` `NOT NULL`. Antes de escribirla: verificar si la migración `20260710043112` dejó la columna poblada en todas las filas. Si hay `NULL`s persistidos, la migración necesita backfill antes del `ALTER`.
- [ ] La rama `target.Score is null` de `MissionRuntimeSnapshot.cs:139` desaparece.
- [ ] **Decidir dónde vive la mitad** `<= 0` **de ese guard.** El guard actual cubre *dos* condiciones y `TreasureHuntTargetSnapshotScoreRequiredException` las señala a ambas. Al mover la positividad a la construcción de `TargetSnapshot`, la invariante de agregado queda sin trabajo — pero la excepción no queda muerta por eso, queda *desubicada*: su nombre dice "required" (nulabilidad) y su referente pasaría a ser una violación de positividad detectada aguas arriba. Opciones: renombrarla a algo tipo `TargetSnapshotScoreMustBePositiveException` y lanzarla desde el constructor, o borrarla e introducir una nueva. Si se borra, actualizar `tests/UnitTests/Domain/Exceptions/ErrorCodeContractTests.cs:73` y el caso de `tests/UnitTests/Domain/Entities/MissionRuntimeSnapshotTests.cs:75`, que hoy la esperan. **Registrar el porqué.**
- [ ] Verificar que no exista ningún `TargetSnapshot` bajo una substage que no sea `TreasureHunt`. El guard de hoy solo alcanza targets de treasure-hunt; un `int` no-nulable con positividad en construcción aplica a *todos* los targets. Si el supuesto no se sostiene, el guard de construcción rompe un camino existente.
- [ ] Suites verdes en `session-operations-service`.

## Lo que este ticket NO hace

Dos de los tres frentes de la versión original de este ticket no sobreviven a la lectura del código. Se retiran, y quedan documentados acá para que no se refilen.

**No agrega cota superior.** La versión original afirmaba *"un* `Score` *de* `101` *o* `5000` *es rechazado, hoy no lo es"*, presentándolo como defecto. No lo es: `ScoreValue.Create` lanza `ScoreValueExceedsMaximumException` por encima de `MaximumPoints = 100`, y ningún camino construye un target fuera de rango. Peor: agregar el techo acá **viola [ADR-0015](<https://github.com/grupo-12-desarrollo-umbral/umbral/blob/develop/backend/docs/adr/0015-per-target-scoring-ownership.md>)**, ratificado después de que este ticket se escribiera. `100` es una constante de negocio de `MissionDesign`. Una segunda copia en el relay rechaza misiones válidas en silencio el día que el tope cambie. `> 0` y no-nulo son sanidad estructural; `<= 100` es regla de negocio con dueño, y el dueño no es `session-operations`.

**No espeja** `ScoreValue` **en** `SessionOperations`**.** El AC original ofrecía esto como opción (a), neutral contra la opción (b). No es neutral: ADR-0015 §Decision ubica explícitamente el cómputo de puntaje fuera de `session-operations`. `int` no-nulable es la única opción consistente con el ADR.

**No toca** `ScoreValue` **de** `mission-design`**,** que ya es correcto.

## Out of scope

* El evento `TargetResolved` y su payload — [DES-42](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-42/hu-31-escaneo-validacion-y-registro-server-side-de-objetivo-qr).
* El ledger `ScoreEntry` — [DES-51](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-51/hu-37-ledger-de-puntaje-por-validaciones-respuestas-y-penalizaciones).
* `mission-design-service/src/Application/Dtos/Trivias/TriviaQuestionDto.cs:9` (`int? ScoreValue = null`) — una asimetría de puntaje nulable *distinta*, del lado de trivia de `mission-design`. Sin ticket. Posiblemente deliberada.

## Notas

Origen: verificación posterior al merge de [DES-86](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-86/refactor-puntaje-por-objetivo-per-target-scorevalue-en-lugar-de-winner) (PR #136, merge commit `995acc8`, 2026-07-10).

No es un bug con repro. Es una nulabilidad que ningún productor puede satisfacer, sostenida por una rama defensiva, sobre un campo que [DES-42](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-42/hu-31-escaneo-validacion-y-registro-server-side-de-objetivo-qr) y [DES-51](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-51/hu-37-ledger-de-puntaje-por-validaciones-respuestas-y-penalizaciones) van a convertir en puntaje real.

## Suggested skills

`ef-core-postgresql` (el `ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL` y su eventual backfill · `dotnet ef migrations add` corre desde la sesión principal, no desde un subagente)
`aspnet-backend-testing` (el destino de `TreasureHuntTargetSnapshotScoreRequiredException` y sus dos tests)

Title: Flaky integration test: AuthoritativeSessionTimerWorkerIntegrationTests.TickAsync_WhenQuestionTimerElapses_ClosesQuestionAndActivatesNext
Description:
## Summary

`AuthoritativeSessionTimerWorkerIntegrationTests.TickAsync_WhenQuestionTimerElapses_ClosesQuestionAndActivatesNext` (session-operations-service, Infrastructure.IntegrationTests) fails intermittently when run as part of the full parallel suite, but passes reliably on isolated re-run.

## Evidence

* Full suite run (`make -C backend test SVC=session-operations-service`): **244/245 passed**, this test failed with:

  ```
  Expected session!.ActiveQuestionIndex to be 1, but found <null>.
  at AuthoritativeSessionTimerWorkerIntegrationTests.cs:line 49
  ```
* Isolated re-run (`dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~TickAsync_WhenQuestionTimerElapses_ClosesQuestionAndActivatesNext`): **passed** (1/1).

## Root cause (suspected)

Timing-sensitive background-worker test. It appears to rely on wall-clock elapsed-timer ticks and loses the race under parallel load, so the timer worker hasn't yet advanced `ActiveQuestionIndex` from null → 1 when the assertion runs. The ~1m suite duration and single-item isolated pass are consistent with a scheduling/timing race rather than a logic bug.

## Not a regression

Surfaced while verifying HU-M2 ([DES-84](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-84/hu-m2-submit-first-answer-from-mobile)) Phase 0, which was a purely additive `Guid TriviaSubstageSnapshotId` field on `QuestionActivatedNotificationDto` / `ActiveQuestionSnapshotDto` — no change to question-index progression logic. The flake is pre-existing.

## Suggested fix

Make the test wait on a deterministic completion signal (poll the projected state / await the worker's tick completion) instead of assuming the tick has landed by assertion time. Avoid wall-clock sleeps.

## Repro

`make -C backend test SVC=session-operations-service` — fails intermittently; re-run the single test to confirm it passes in isolation.

Title: EN-M1 — Mobile trivia contract spike (display + submit)
Description:
## Parent

Local plan: `mobile/plans/post-hu-34a-mobile-trivia-breakdown.md` (section `EN-M1 — Mobile gameplay contract spike`).

Backing backend work, all shipped: `DES-78` (HU-33A — synchronized trivia orchestration), `DES-45` (HU-33B — round close + final results), `DES-30`/`DES-77` (HU-22 — authoritative session timer), and now `DES-46` **(HU-34 — first-valid-answer registration + rejection), merged 2026-07-10 (PR #133)**.

## What to build

Freeze the participant-facing realtime + REST contract for `team-space` so the mobile app implements against verified backend shapes instead of guessed DTOs and event names. This is the gating enabler for `HU-M1` (display), `HU-M3` (closed state) and `HU-M2` (submit).

> **Rewritten 2026-07-10.** The original spike scoped *display only* and put submit out of scope because `DES-46` was unstarted. `DES-46` has shipped, so its answer contract exists and this spike freezes it too — that is why `DES-84`'s "verify against HU-34 output" clause moved here. The original also asserted a missing-broadcast gap that does not exist; see §"Correction". Verified against code, 2026-07-10.

## Display contract — verify and type

* **Active-question broadcast** — `QuestionActivatedNotificationDto` via the `QuestionActivated` SignalR method, pushed to the participant-visible `live-session:{liveSessionId}` group (`SignalRSessionQuestionBroadcaster.cs:24-31`). Fields: `LiveSessionId`, `QuestionIndex`, `SequenceOrder`, `Prompt`, `Options` (read-only list), `TimeLimitSeconds`, `ActivatedAt`. **Not yet typed on mobile — add it.**
* **Active-question REST snapshot** — `ActiveQuestionSnapshotDto` nested in `SessionTimerSnapshotDto`, from `GET /sessions/{liveSessionId}/participants/timer?teamId=&token=` (`Participant` policy). Adds `RemainingSeconds` over the broadcast. Null when no question is active. This is the **reconnect/late-join** path — the broadcast is the steady-state path.
* **Countdown broadcast** — `SessionTimerUpdatedNotificationDto` via `SessionTimerUpdated`. Timer only; already typed in `mobile/src/lib/realtime/timer-types.ts` — confirm no drift.
* **Question-closed broadcast** — `QuestionClosedNotificationDto` via `QuestionClosed` (participant group). Fields: `LiveSessionId`, `QuestionIndex`, `ClosedAt`, `WasExpiredByTimer`. **Not yet typed on mobile — add it.**
* **Substage-advanced broadcast** — `SubstageAdvancedNotificationDto` via `SubstageAdvanced` (participant group). Confirm shape and type if `HU-M1`/`HU-M3` need it.
* **Session-state broadcast** — `SessionStateChangedNotificationDto` via `SessionStateChanged`; already typed on mobile — confirm no drift.

## Submit contract — verify and type (new — folded in from [DES-84](https://linear.app/desarrollo-equipo-12/issue/DES-84/hu-m2-submit-first-answer-from-mobile))

Frozen by `DES-46`; recorded in `backend/docs/prompt_example_feature_hu34.md` §9. This spike transcribes it, it does not re-derive it.

* **Endpoint** — `POST /sessions/{liveSessionId}/participants/answers`, `Participant` policy (`SessionsController.cs:162`).
* **Request** — `SubmitTriviaAnswerRequest`: `TeamId`, `TriviaSubstageSnapshotId`, `QuestionSequenceOrder`, `SelectedOptionSequenceOrder`, `Token?` (`SessionsController.cs:247`).
* **Accepted response (200)** — `SubmitTriviaAnswerResultDto`: `LiveSessionId`, `TeamId`, `TriviaSubstageSnapshotId`, `QuestionSequenceOrder`, `AnsweredAt`. **Acceptance metadata only** — no `IsCorrect`, no `ScoreValue`, no selected option. Correctness/points are withheld from every realtime surface by design (fairness) and surface only after close (HU-35) / downstream scoring (HU-37).
* **Rejections** — RFC 7807 ProblemDetails via the global handler, each with a stable `reasonCode` slug:
  * `late-trivia-answer` — after the timer window closed
  * `duplicate-trivia-answer` — team already answered this question
  * `trivia-answer-requires-active-question` — no active question
  * `trivia-answer-requires-active-session` — session not `Active`
  * `trivia-answer-requires-trivia-substage` — active substage is not trivia
  * `invalid-trivia-answer-option` — option order not valid for the question
  * `answer-submitter-is-not-session-participant` — forbidden / wrong-team
* **Operator-only signal** — `TeamAnsweredNotificationDto` via `TeamAnswered`, broadcast to the operator-only group, **not** the participant group. Deliberately carries no correctness/score/option. The mobile participant client does **not** consume it — noted so `HU-M2` does not wire to it by mistake. It belongs to `DES-49` (web operator monitor).

## Correction — the "missing QuestionOpened broadcast" gap does not exist

The original spike documented that there is *no* `QuestionOpened`/`ActiveQuestionActivated` broadcast and that prompt/options are reachable only via REST, then asked the spike to choose a REST-fallback fetch strategy. **That is wrong as of the current code.** `QuestionActivated` (above) pushes `Prompt` + `Options` to the participant group on activation. The REST snapshot is the reconnect/late-join path, not the only path. No new backend broadcast needs proposing.

## Real gap to document instead — sourcing `TriviaSubstageSnapshotId` for submit

Submit **requires** `TriviaSubstageSnapshotId`, but **neither** `QuestionActivatedNotificationDto` **nor** `ActiveQuestionSnapshotDto` carries it — both key the question by `(QuestionIndex, SequenceOrder)` only. The mobile client must obtain the substage snapshot id from some already-available surface (e.g. the session/substage snapshot the team joined against) or the spike proposes adding it to the active-question shapes in a downstream backend ticket. **Pick the smallest honest strategy that does not invent backend behavior, and record the trade-off.** This replaces the (non-existent) fetch-strategy gap as the spike's one open decision.

## Mobile deliverables

* Typed DTOs under `mobile/src/lib/realtime/` (or a sibling for REST) mirroring: `QuestionActivatedNotificationDto`, `QuestionClosedNotificationDto`, `ActiveQuestionSnapshotDto`, the submit request/result shapes, and the rejection `reasonCode` set.
* Extend `SessionsHubClient` (`mobile/src/lib/realtime/sessions-hub.ts`) with `onQuestionActivated` and `onQuestionClosed` handlers returning an unsubscribe, mirroring the existing `onTimerUpdated`/`onStateChanged` pattern.
* A submit helper (or a documented note on where it should live) for `POST …/participants/answers`, plus a typed rejection-reason union.
* A contract note under `mobile/docs/` recording every verified shape above, the chosen `TriviaSubstageSnapshotId` sourcing strategy and its trade-off, and any drift found against existing mobile types.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mobile has typed DTOs mirroring `QuestionActivatedNotificationDto`, `QuestionClosedNotificationDto`, and `ActiveQuestionSnapshotDto`.
- [ ] Mobile has typed request/result DTOs for the submit endpoint and a typed union of the seven rejection `reasonCode` slugs.
- [ ] `SessionsHubClient` exposes `onQuestionActivated` and `onQuestionClosed`, each returning an unsubscribe, consistent with `onTimerUpdated`/`onStateChanged`.
- [ ] The countdown (`SessionTimerUpdated`) and session-state (`SessionStateChanged`) broadcasts are confirmed unchanged or any drift is documented.
- [ ] The contract note records the chosen `TriviaSubstageSnapshotId` sourcing strategy and its trade-off.
- [ ] No invented backend shapes — every typed DTO maps to a real backend DTO, broadcast, or endpoint documented in the note.
- [ ] The note states explicitly that `TeamAnswered` is operator-only and the participant client does not consume it.

## Blocked by

None — every backend dependency has shipped. `HU-22` (`DES-30`/`DES-77`), `HU-33A` (`DES-78`), `HU-33B` (`DES-45`), and `HU-34` (`DES-46`, PR #133) are all done. This spike now freezes **both** the display and the submit contract, so `DES-84` no longer verifies backend shapes — it consumes this note.

Title: Bootstrap MassTransit + RabbitMQ and publish QuestionClosed end-to-end
Description:
## What to build

Introduce MassTransit as the messaging layer for `session-operations-service`, backed by the RabbitMQ transport, and prove the full publish path end-to-end with the **first** integration event: `QuestionClosedIntegrationEvent`.

Today the service publishes with a hand-rolled `RabbitMqIntegrationEventPublisher` (RabbitMQ.Client 7.1.2) behind the `IIntegrationEventPublisher` seam. This slice stands up the standard MassTransit stack **alongside** that code (the old publisher stays for the other two events until later slices) and migrates only the `QuestionClosed` flow so the whole vertical path — contract → publish → RabbitMQ → bound consumer — is demonstrable.

Approach (agreed conventions):

* Register the bus with the canonical `builder.Services.AddMassTransit(x => x.UsingRabbitMq(...))`. No custom topology or formatters.
* Publish via MassTransit's standard `IPublishEndpoint.Publish(...)` directly from the MediatR `INotificationHandler` (`PublishQuestionClosedIntegrationEventHandler`). We are **not** keeping the `IIntegrationEventPublisher` abstraction for the migrated path — the handler uses `IPublishEndpoint` directly, which is the idiomatic MassTransit pattern.
* **MassTransit-native topology**, but give the message a short, readable exchange name using the built-in `[EntityName("session-question-closed")]` attribute on the `QuestionClosedIntegrationEvent` record. This keeps the RabbitMQ management UI showing a domain-meaningful exchange name (matching the old `session.question.closed` spirit) instead of the full C# type name — a one-attribute, fully-documented tweak.
* Replace the hardcoded option defaults with **real configuration**: bind RabbitMQ host/port/vhost/credentials from `appsettings.json` + environment variables, and add the corresponding `RabbitMq__*` (or MassTransit) env vars to `backend/docker-compose.yml` for the `session-operations` service, pointing at the existing `rabbitmq` compose service.

MassTransit's default behavior gives a dead-letter `<queue>_error` queue automatically — no extra configuration needed. Do **not** add a transactional outbox or custom retry policy in this slice (deferred as out of scope).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `MassTransit` and `MassTransit.RabbitMQ` package references are added (version pinned centrally in `Directory.Packages.props`).
- [ ] The bus is registered with `AddMassTransit(...).UsingRabbitMq(...)` and started via the Generic Host (bus starts/stops with the app).
- [ ] RabbitMQ connection settings are read from configuration (appsettings + env vars), not hardcoded defaults; docker-compose passes the broker host/credentials to the service.
- [ ] `QuestionClosedIntegrationEvent` is published through `IPublishEndpoint.Publish(...)` from its MediatR handler; the message carries the `[EntityName("session-question-closed")]` exchange name.
- [ ] An integration test (Testcontainers.RabbitMq) spins up a broker, publishes a `QuestionClosed` event through the real handler/bus, and asserts a bound consumer/queue receives it. Test skips gracefully when Docker is unavailable, matching the existing test's behavior.
- [ ] The `RabbitMq` management UI shows a `session-question-closed` exchange (verified manually or documented in the PR).
- [ ] The old hand-rolled publisher still handles the other two events (no regression); build and existing tests pass.

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately.

Implement the third `MissionDesign` vertical slice that hardens mission hierarchy rules and source-readiness validation.
